title: Minimal Polynomial Reduction and Annihilator Theory
description: The minimal polynomial gives an optimal polynomial reduction for matrix evaluation, tighter than the characteristic polynomial. For any polynomial f and matrix M, aeval M f = aeval M (f mod minpoly(M)). The annihilator ideal of M is generated by the minimal polynomial.

overview.historicalContext:
The minimal polynomial of a matrix is the monic polynomial of least degree that annihilates it. While the Cayley-Hamilton theorem shows every matrix is annihilated by its characteristic polynomial (degree n), the minimal polynomial can have much smaller degree. For a scalar matrix cI, the minimal polynomial is just (X - c) regardless of n.

The relationship between the minimal and characteristic polynomials is central to the theory of canonical forms: the Jordan normal form is determined by the minimal polynomial together with the elementary divisors, and a matrix is nonderogatory (has a single Jordan block per eigenvalue) precisely when its minimal polynomial equals its characteristic polynomial.

This formalization extends the charpoly reduction (OQ-02) by proving the tighter minpoly reduction and fully characterizing the annihilator ideal.
overview.problemStatement:
**Minimal Polynomial Reduction Theorem**: For any polynomial f and n x n matrix M:

aeval M f = aeval M (f mod minpoly(M))

where the remainder has degree < deg(minpoly) <= n.

**Annihilator Ideal**: A polynomial annihilates M if and only if it is a multiple of the minimal polynomial. This characterizes the kernel of the evaluation map as a principal ideal.

**Optimality**: Since minpoly divides charpoly, this reduction is at least as tight as (and potentially tighter than) the characteristic polynomial reduction.
overview.proofStrategy:
The proof uses the division algorithm for monic polynomials. Since minpoly(M) is monic, any polynomial f decomposes as f = q * minpoly(M) + r where deg(r) < deg(minpoly). Evaluating at M and using minpoly.aeval (minpoly(M) annihilates M) yields aeval M f = aeval M r.

The annihilator characterization follows from Mathlib's minpoly.dvd (any annihilating polynomial is divisible by minpoly) and the converse (multiples of minpoly annihilate M). The comparison with charpoly reduction follows from the divisibility minpoly | charpoly.
keyInsights: The minimal polynomial generates the annihilator ideal: aeval M f = 0 iff minpoly divides f
Minpoly reduction is tighter than charpoly reduction since deg(minpoly) <= deg(charpoly) = n
Two polynomials evaluate to the same matrix iff they are congruent modulo the minimal polynomial
For derogatory matrices (minpoly != charpoly), the minpoly gives strictly better reduction bounds
Idempotent matrices have minpoly dividing X(X-1), involutory matrices have minpoly dividing X^2-1
Nilpotent matrices have minpoly = X^d, so M^d = 0 with d = deg(minpoly) <= n

sections.title: Minimal Polynomial Reduction
sections.summary: Core result: aeval M f = aeval M (f mod minpoly). Uses division algorithm and minpoly annihilation.

sections.title: Degree Bounds from Minimal Polynomial
sections.summary: The reduced polynomial has degree < deg(minpoly) <= n, potentially tighter than charpoly bound.

sections.title: The Annihilator Ideal
sections.summary: The annihilator is a principal ideal generated by minpoly. Closure under addition and multiplication.

sections.title: Congruence via Minimal Polynomial
sections.summary: Two polynomials evaluate identically iff congruent mod minpoly, a finer equivalence than charpoly.

sections.title: Power Reduction via Minimal Polynomial
sections.summary: Matrix powers M^k reduce mod minpoly. Every polynomial expression representable in degree < deg(minpoly).

sections.title: Comparison with Characteristic Polynomial
sections.summary: Minpoly degree <= charpoly degree = n. Charpoly reduction refines to minpoly reduction.

sections.title: Special Cases
sections.summary: Scalar matrices, identity, zero matrix. Concrete examples of minpoly being smaller than charpoly.

sections.title: Nilpotent Matrices
sections.summary: Nilpotent matrices via minpoly: if minpoly = X^d then M^d = 0 and higher powers vanish.

sections.title: Idempotent and Involutory Matrices
sections.summary: Idempotent M (M^2 = M): minpoly divides X^2 - X. Involutory M (M^2 = I): minpoly divides X^2 - 1.

conclusion.summary: This formalization proves the minimal polynomial reduction theorem and fully characterizes the annihilator ideal. All 25+ theorems are fully proved (0 sorries), establishing the minimal polynomial as the optimal reduction tool for matrix polynomial evaluation.
conclusion.implications:
**Computational Efficiency**: Matrix function computation via minpoly requires fewer terms than charpoly, especially for derogatory matrices.

**Control Theory**: A system is controllable/observable iff its minpoly equals its charpoly (nonderogatory).

**Jordan Form**: The minpoly encodes the sizes of the largest Jordan blocks per eigenvalue.

**Abstract Algebra**: The evaluation map K[X] -> End(V) has kernel (minpoly), yielding K[X]/(minpoly) as the generated subalgebra.
openQuestions: Can we formalize the relationship between minpoly and Jordan canonical form in Lean?
How does the minimal polynomial interact with matrix similarity and conjugacy?
